q.t: What are the 7 main swaras?
o: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni
Do Re Mi Fa So La Ti
Sa Ga Re Ma Dha Pa Ni
C D E F G A B
q.e: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni, then Sa again.

q.t: In Indian music, Sa is…
o: whatever note you choose as home
q.e: Singers tune Sa to their own voice.

q.t: With Sa = C, what is Pa?
q.e: Pa is the 5th: C → G.

q.t: With Sa = C, what is Ga?
q.e: Shuddh Ga is the major 3rd: C → E.

q.t: What does komal mean?
q.e: Komal = soft — a half step lower.

q.t: What does teevra mean?
q.e: Teevra = sharp — only Ma can be teevra.

q.t: Which two swaras never change?
q.e: Sa and Pa are achal (fixed).

q.t: How many swaras are there counting komal and teevra?
q.e: 7 shuddh + 4 komal + 1 teevra = 12 — the same as the 12 Western notes.

q.t: What instrument plays the drone of Sa and Pa?
q.e: The tanpura holds Sa and Pa steadily under the music.

q.t: Bilawal thaat is the same as which Western scale?
q.e: S R G M P D N — all shuddh = major.

q.t: With Sa = C, what is teevra Ma?
q.e: Ma = F; teevra raises it a half step to F♯.

q.t: With Sa = C, what is komal Ni?
q.e: Ni = B; komal lowers it to B♭.

q.t: With Sa = C, what is komal Ga?
q.e: Ga = E; komal = E♭.

q.t: With Sa = C, what is Dha?
q.e: Dha is the 6th: C → A.

q.t: Why are Sa and Pa fixed?
o: They are the drone — home and its perfect 5th
q.e: The smoothest pair after the octave — the steady floor of every raag.

q.t: Raag Bhupali uses which swaras?
o: S R G M P D N
S r g M P d n
q.e: No Ma, no Ni.

q.t: What is the aaroh of a raag?
q.e: Aaroh = ascent; avroh = descent.

q.t: Raag Yaman uses which special swara?
q.e: Teevra Ma gives Yaman its bright, lifted sound.

q.t: A dot below a swara means…
q.e: Dot below = mandra; dot above = taar.

q.t: Why does sargam work like scale step numbers?
o: Each name is a position from home
Each name is a fixed pitch
q.e: Sa = step 1, Pa = step 5, wherever Sa is.

q.t: With Sa = D, what is Ga?
q.e: 4 half steps up from D: D♯, E, F, F♯.

q.t: With Sa = D, what is Pa?
q.e: 7 half steps up from D = A.

q.t: With Sa = E, what is Re?
q.e: 2 half steps up from E: F, F♯.

q.t: With Sa = A, what is Ma?
q.e: 5 half steps up from A: A♯, B, C, C♯, D.

q.t: Asavari thaat (S R g M P d n) is the same as…
q.e: Komal Ga, Dha and Ni = the minor 3rd, 6th and 7th.

q.t: Kalyan thaat is the major scale with…
q.e: S R G M' P D N — Western name Lydian.

q.t: Khamaj thaat is the major scale with…
q.e: S R G M P D n — Mixolydian.

q.t: Why does Bhupali sound calm?
o: Leaving out Ma and Ni removes the half steps
q.e: Ga–Ma and Ni–Sa are the half steps; without Ma and Ni none remain.

q.t: Yaman's aaroh starts from the lower Ni. With Sa = C, that note is…
q.e: Ni = B, one octave down (A string fret 2 on the guitar).

q.t: Why does playing a komal Ga as shuddh Ga ruin a tune?
o: It changes a minor 3rd into a major 3rd
q.e: Minor 3rd vs major 3rd — the whole mood flips.

q.t: With Sa = G, what is komal Ni?
q.e: Ni = F♯ (11 up); komal = F (10 up).

q.t: With Sa = E, what is teevra Ma?
q.e: Ma = A (5 up); teevra = A♯ (6 up).

q.t: With Sa = C, Bhupali's notes are…
q.e: S R G P D → C D E G A.

q.t: With Sa = C, Yaman's aaroh (,N R G M' D N S') is…
o: B D E F♯ A B C
B D E F A B C
C D E F♯ G A B
B C D E F♯ A C
q.e: Lower Ni B, then Re D, Ga E, teevra Ma F♯, Dha A, Ni B, Sa C.

q.t: Bhairavi thaat (S r g M P d n) — how many swaras are komal?
q.e: Re, Ga, Dha and Ni are all komal.

q.t: Kafi thaat (S R g M P D n) matches which Western scale?
q.e: Komal Ga and Ni with shuddh Dha = Dorian.

q.t: In sargam, the interval Sa → teevra Ma is how many half steps?
q.e: Ma is 5; teevra adds 1 = 6 — a tritone.

q.t: Why choose Sa = E on the guitar?
o: Sa is the open low E — lots of open strings
E is the only allowed Sa
It avoids all sharps in every raag
q.e: An open-string Sa can ring as a drone while you play.

q.t: A raag isn't only a set of notes. What else defines it?
o: Rules about how to move through the notes
q.e: E.g. Yaman's aaroh starts from lower Ni and moves around Sa.

q.t: Why do some thaats match Western scales exactly?
o: Both pick 7 of the same 12 notes
They have different numbers of notes
q.e: Same 7 out of 12 → same scale, two names.
